clauses.description: The clauses and terms defined in the contract.

meetingTime.description: Scheduled meeting time for the contract. (date-time)

status.description: The status of the contract (e.g., draft, active, completed, cancelled).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Client entity.

email.description: The email address of the client.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The email address of the user.

definition.description: Stores contract documents owned by a specific user. The path enforces ownership and simplifies security rules.

params.name: userId
params.description: The ID of the user who owns the contract.

params.name: contractId
params.description: The ID of the contract document.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to provide a secure and scalable solution for managing contracts and clients. It leverages path-based ownership and denormalization to ensure authorization independence. The `/users/{userId}/contracts/{contractId}` path establishes clear ownership. The `contracts` collection is nested under the `users` collection, ensuring that each contract is associated with a specific user, thus satisfying the user's request. The security rules in the request only permit reading contracts based on the UID, so the data structure is created to be like that.

This structure inherently supports QAPs by segregating contracts based on user ownership. Listing contracts is secure because the list operation is always scoped to a specific user, and only that user can access their contracts.
